soil_c_evidence: Poeplau & Don 0.32 Mg C/ha/yr (n=139 plots); Vicente-Vicente 1.1 olive / 0.78 vineyard / 2.0 almond t C/ha/yr
soil_c_note: Four rows, two meta-analyses, all positive. Matches Table 6. Poeplau cautions N2O and albedo are excluded, and the cover-crop N2O rows here suggest that omission is not conservative.
n2o_direction: increase or variable, NOT the predicted decrease
n2o_evidence: Basche 60% of 106 observations positive; Li 2023 variable; Li 2024 legume cover crops increased N2O
n2o_note: TABLE 6 CONTRADICTED. Three independent sources against the predicted decrease; David has confirmed this was an error and it should read increase/variable. Full-year LRRs sit near zero, so the net effect is closer to neutral than to a reduction.
ch4_note: No evidence in the group library. The only item pairing cover crops with methane is De Gryze, which David excluded as primarily a modelling study. The single genuinely empty cell.

soil_c_evidence: Vicente-Vicente 5.3 t C/ha/yr for organic amendments in olive orchards (51 references)
soil_c_note: Matches Table 6, but rests on one meta-analysis and one cropping system. Sequestration efficiency exceeded 100%, which the authors attribute to unaccounted inputs plus reduced erosion.
n2o_evidence: Ma 2021: all straw treatments below control, CK > SM > S > SI > SB
n2o_note: TABLE 6 CONTRADICTED, but by a single two-season experiment in Chinese cotton, so tier 2. Not enough to overturn the hypothesis; enough to stop calling it settled. Needs a synthesis.
ch4_direction: depends on the form of carbon added
ch4_evidence: Ma 2021: CH4 tracks the CO2 response; raw straw and straw+inoculant increased GWP, biochar decreased it 17.9-19.8%
ch4_note: At EQUAL carbon input the sign depends on form, not amount. A statewide non-crop-C scenario that does not distinguish straw from biochar cannot be benchmarked against this.

soil_c_direction: increase, but shallow-sampling and offset caveats
soil_c_evidence: Robertson 30 g C/m2/yr; Six Table 1 SOC term -710 to -815 kg CO2-eq/ha/yr
soil_c_note: Direction is consistent, but Robertson is a single experiment sampled at 0-7.5 cm and Snyder notes shallow sampling can overstate no-till gains. Six shows the SOC gain is partly offset by N2O in net GWP terms.
n2o_evidence: van Kessel no overall effect (239 comparisons); Li 2023 -11% (95% CI -19 to -1); Snyder 0.68+/-0.57 vs 0.95+/-0.98; van Kessel +57% under 10 yr dry, -27% after
n2o_note: Two meta-analyses disagree, and the sign flips with adoption age. Snyder's inventory contrast has heavily overlapping standard deviations. No defensible single direction.
ch4_evidence: Six 0.6 +/- 0.1 kg CH4/ha/yr uptake, identical in both climates and at 5, 10 and 20 years
ch4_note: Table 6 marks this uncertain; the evidence is actually consistent, just small: -13 kg CO2-eq/ha/yr, negligible beside the SOC and N2O terms.

soil_c_direction: slows loss, does not reverse it
soil_c_evidence: Snyder/Wilts 30-year Minnesota: corn-derived SOC 17.0 / 13.0 / 10.1 t/ha at 168 / 83 / 0 kg N/ha/yr
soil_c_note: Matches Table 6's uncertain. Critically, total SOC DECLINED at every N rate; fertilisation only slowed the decline. Reading this as sequestration would be wrong.
n2o_evidence: 17 rows. IPCC EF1 0.010 aggregated, 0.005 dry, 0.016 wet synthetic; Cayuela EF_Med 0.5%; Liu EFc 2.58%; Leschinsky says even 0.5% overestimates for organic fertiliser
n2o_note: The best-supported cell. Also the clearest California finding: IPCC's dry-climate EF (0.005) and Cayuela's Mediterranean EF (0.5%) agree independently, and Leschinsky argues even that is high. Condition on irrigation, crop and N rate: Cayuela's advantage disappears above 400 kg N/ha.
ch4_evidence: Snyder: non-rice soils are a CH4 sink but weaker than native soils; nitrification inhibitors inhibit CH4 oxidation
ch4_note: No pooled effect size exists in the library. A review statement and a second-hand result. Direction is consistent with Table 6's uncertain, but nothing here is usable as a quantitative benchmark.

soil_c_evidence: Kirk: flooded rice on Delta peat loses 1149-2473 kg C/ha/yr against 3700-8600 for drained aerobic cropping
soil_c_note: Flooding roughly halves the loss but the soil remains a net source. Against drained cropland flooding helps; against an undrained baseline it still loses carbon. That is exactly why Table 6 marks it uncertain. Same peat as US-Twt.
n2o_direction: draining raises N2O; flooding lowers it
n2o_evidence: Jiang +105% N2O under non-continuous flooding; IPCC EF1FR continuous 0.003 vs drained 0.005; Cayuela flooded rice 0.19%; Li 2024 deficit irrigation -62%
n2o_note: Four sources agree in direction, so this is better supported than Table 6's uncertain suggests. But N2O contributes only 12% of combined GWP (Jiang), so the tradeoff does not overturn the CH4 benefit. Worse in high-SOC soils and with manure, which describes Delta peat.
ch4_direction: strong decrease when flooding is reduced
ch4_evidence: Jiang -53% CH4 under non-continuous flooding (201 paired observations, 52 studies); net GWP -44%, yield -3.6%
ch4_note: Matches Table 6's strong decrease. Dose-dependent: the reduction grows with the number of drying events and unflooded days. Jiang also proposes revising the IPCC scaling factors from 0.6 to 0.67 (single drying) and 0.52 to 0.36 (multiple).

soil_c_direction: increase, but only after about ten years
soil_c_evidence: Siddique +16.6% vs monoculture, +23.1% vs rotation at 0-30 cm; negative under 5 years; plateau near 20 years
soil_c_note: Table 6's strong increase holds only in the long run. Under 5 years the effect is NEGATIVE. Same time-dependence as tillage, so a statewide comparison must condition on stand age.
n2o_direction: large source measured where a decrease was predicted
n2o_evidence: Anthony 624 +/- 28 mg N2O/m2/yr at US-Bi1, offsetting the ecosystem carbon sink by up to 14%
n2o_note: TABLE 6 CONTRADICTED, and at one of our own cal/val sites. A perennial N-fixer is a large N2O source. Tier 2 (one site) but directly checkable. Hot moments are 1% of measurements and up to 57% of the annual flux, so an annual mean is a weak test of the mechanism.
ch4_evidence: Robertson: late successional system GWP neutral because of significant methane oxidation
ch4_note: Consistent with Table 6's uncertain. Tier 2, one experiment, and the comparison is unmanaged succession rather than a perennial crop.
